source.check: Castledawson count read in the News-Letter of 2 June 1961; the 24 unopposed returns read in the Mid-Ulster Mail nomination report of 20 May 1961, p. 1 (page image).

note: Triennial election of Magherafelt Rural District Council, polled Thursday 1 June 1961. Only Castledawson was contested: Mr. Hugh M'Master, who had represented the division for more than thirty years as an official Unionist, stood after Mr. Samuel K. Dunlop was chosen as the Unionist candidate, and beat Dunlop by 76 votes. Twenty-four divisions were filled unopposed (Mid-Ulster Mail, 20 May 1961, p. 1). No one was nominated for Draperstown (retiring member Patrick Trolan), so that seat was not filled at the election and is not recorded here. The Returning Officer's notice of the result (Mid-Ulster Mail, 10 June 1961, p. 10) leaves Draperstown blank in every column, with no member deemed re-elected; under the 1949 regulations a seat with no eligible retiring member stayed unfilled until the next election, and the Mid-Ulster Mail of 23 May 1964, p. 1, confirms that Draperstown 'has not had a representative on the Council for the past three years as no candidate was nominated at the last election' (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Printed: 'Mr. M'Master received 297 votes against Mr. Dunlop's 221.'
